Over the past few months, Kim has been increasingly seen with a group of older teenagers associated with criminal networks. Kim was recently arrested by the police on suspicion of participating in a villa burglary.

Upon receiving this information, my first step would be to assess whether Kim needs immediate protection or support from social services. After careful evaluation, I concluded that no immediate intervention was necessary. I then contacted Kim’s parents to inform them about the information provided by the police and invited them to a meeting along with Kim.

Concern Reports and Reporting Obligations':Young people have the right to receive proper care, even if their parents or guardians are not always able to ensure it. Therefore, anyone who is concerned about a young person can report it to social services. This is called a Concern Report.
Anyone can submit a Concern Report, and some adults are legally obligated to do so. For example, if you are worried about a friend or sibling, you can file a Concern Report with social services (often referred to as "soc"). If you prefer, you can report anonymously.
According to the law, adults who believe that someone under the age of 18 is in danger must report it. This is known as the Reporting Obligation. This applies to adults working in sectors such as schools, healthcare, or law enforcement.
Hello everyone, I’m glad you could come. Let’s all sit down and have a conversation about this.
Hello.
Hello, we really need some advice.
I think I’m fine. There’s nothing to talk about.
Hey Kim, we talked about this before.
No need to be nervous. For now, we’re just having a simple conversation.
Kim, some things have happened recently, right? We received a report from the police.
They’re worried that you might get into trouble that could harm yourself or others. We really want to offer our support. Can we talk about it?"
(Her eyes waver for a moment but quickly return to a firm look) I can take responsibility for what I do. I don’t need anyone’s help.
Kim! What responsibility can you take? Haven’t you done enough already?
Hanging out with those gang members every day, doing all sorts of shady things! Do you have any idea how worried we are? Your mother can’t even sleep at night!
Alright, alright, that’s enough.
I never asked you to do that. You don’t need to worry about me.
Kim! Why won’t you just listen?
Everyone, please calm down and listen to me.
Kim, your father is right. You’re being too disobedient.
Kim’s father, don’t be too harsh. The child is struggling too.
Arguing won’t solve anything. We’re here today not to fight, but to have a conversation. Let’s all take a deep breath and calm down, alright? We’ll take it slow.
Who are you anyway? What does this have to do with you? You’re just an outsider sticking your nose into our business!
Kim!
I understand that everyone is upset right now, but please try to stay calm.
We have coffee and some snacks. How about we sit down and have a cup of coffee together?

While we had coffee, we chatted casually for a while. Kim chose to sit aside, scrolling through her phone. Her parents looked exhausted. I did my best to engage them in small talk, hoping to lift their spirits a little. But I knew what they truly needed was a way to help Kim.
Sensing that Kim’s resistance might be due to her parents' presence, I decided it would be best to have a one-on-one conversation with her.
(Looking down, typing on her phone)
Kim, would you like to have a chat with me?
About what?
About yourself — what you’re thinking. No pressure. Everything we talk about will remain strictly confidential.
What do you like to do in your free time?
I usually hang out with my friends, just messing around and chatting.
Do you enjoy spending time with them?
I… I guess. They’re pretty cool. Being with them feels freeing — much better than being stuck at home. At home, it’s all rules and nagging. It’s boring.
I heard that some of your friends might be involved with gangs. Do you ever worry that something bad might happen to you?
I… Most of them are good people. But yeah, sometimes things do go too far. I guess I do get scared sometimes, but I don’t want to seem weak.
But you know, friends are supposed to have each other’s backs. And like I said, I’m willing to take responsibility for what I do.
It sounds like you’re a very responsible person.
Of course! Everyone trusts me. I really like the feeling of being trusted. My parents… they never trust me. I don’t think there’s any point talking to them.
You feel like they don’t trust or understand you, right?
Exactly! They think I’m crazy for hanging out with my friends. My dad says I’m talking nonsense when I say I’m happy with them.
He always says that if I keep this up, I’ll either get killed, end up in jail, or end up pregnant. They never understand how I feel.
You know, I think they’re genuinely concerned about you. It’s not out of malice — I can see that.
I’m not saying they don’t care… they just don’t understand.
It seems like there are some communication issues between you and your parents. That’s something we can work on step by step.
But for now, they are worried that your friends might have a bad influence on you. You even mentioned earlier that sometimes things get a little out of hand, didn’t you?
I… I don’t know.
I’m here today because I want to help you. If you’re willing, I’d like to work with you to find a solution.
I… I don’t know if there’s really a solution. But if you have any ideas, I… I’m willing to listen.

The meeting concluded. Afterward, considering the information provided by the police and what Kim and her parents shared, I determined that further investigation into Kim’s situation and support needs was necessary.

I initiated the investigation and, at the beginning of the process, worked with Kim and her parents to develop a plan. Together, we identified individuals within the family’s social network who might have valuable insights for the investigation. We also explored what kind of support the family could receive from their network.
I believe Kim currently has three main needs. The first need is:
Lacks proper reasoning and needs stricter discipline
Feels too restricted, should set her free
Poor mutual understanding between Kim and her parents

Kim's primary need is to improve communication with her parents. Both sides struggle to understand each other, which needs to be resolved through long-term effort. Stricter control could increase Kim's rebellious tendencies, while giving her complete freedom might lead to even worse outcomes.
If we want to start solving the problem immediately, the second short-term need is:
A new environment where Kim can feel free
Improving the family environment to help Kim feel the warmth of home
Educating and criticizing the gang to create a better environment

In the short term, creating a new environment where Kim can feel a sense of freedom is essential. Improving the family environment will likely take time and effort, and educating the gang is too idealistic to be a realistic solution.
The third short-term need is:
Asking teachers to assign Kim more homework to occupy her free time
Finding other activities for Kim during her free time
Introducing Kim to a boyfriend

The most appropriate third need is to find alternative activities for Kim during her free time instead of associating with the gang. These activities should provide her with a sense of belonging and ideally involve guidance from responsible individuals who can act as role models.

We held several additional meetings with Kim and her family to discuss these needs. Kim agreed with our perspective. During this time, we identified several contacts who can offer support, and Kim expressed willingness to try. And she wants you to recommend one option for her.
Kim's uncle's restaurant - Kim works as a dishwasher in the kitchen
Kim's aunt's stable - Kim takes care of the horses at the stable
Kim's teacher - Kim volunteers at school's community center

I recommended that Kim work at her uncle's restaurant to fill her free time. Under her uncle's supervision, this job could serve as a good regulatory measure. Initially, Kim found that the new environment helped her, but after a while, she felt the restaurant's rules and repetitive work restricted her freedom, and it didn’t provide her with the sense of recognition she needed.

After a conflict with the restaurant supervisor, she stopped going to the restaurant. Her parents later reported that she was hanging out with gang members again. I tried to contact Kim and persuade her to try a new approach, but she refused. The case ended.

I recommended that Kim work at her aunt's stable, as Kim loves animals and was happy to help. Kim’s aunt occasionally joined her in taking care of the horses, which provided some structure for Kim. The praise from her aunt also gave Kim some of the recognition she needed. Kim found the rural environment quite freeing, but over time, she began to feel lonely.

Her animal friends couldn’t chat or drink beer with her, so she started to miss her previous friends. Kim continued to help at the stable on weekends, but her parents reported that she was still hanging out with gang members. I contacted Kim, and she said her situation was fine and that she didn’t need further help. I continued to encourage her, but she refused. The case ended.

I recommended that Kim volunteer at the community center through her teacher. Kim was safe at school, and her teacher played a good regulatory role. The new environment at the community center made her feel free, and the volunteer work gave her a lot of recognition. She began dedicating more and more time to it.

Through her teacher's introduction and her own interactions, Kim met a lot of new people and made new friends. Kim's parents reported that she no longer participated in gang activities. While she still spent a lot of time away from home, her parents were satisfied and thanked me. I believe the communication issues between Kim and her family still need long-term effort, so I recommended a family therapist. Kim's parents thanked me, and the case ended.
A few months later, Kim's mother called me.
Hi, how are you? This is Kim's mom, Claire.
Hi Claire, how have you been?
We're doing great! We're having a barbecue, with Kim, her dad, and Kim's new friends. We're really happy, and I thought of you.
None of this would have been possible without your help.
That's great! I'm so glad to hear that.
(Speaking off the phone) What's up, Kim? Do you want to say something?
long time no hear! I just want to say, the advice you gave me was really cool. I've made some great friends, and they all support me.
The family therapist you recommended was awesome, and my parents finally started listening to me. Alright, I’m going to eat some barbecue now. Take care of yourself, stay cool, alright?
Haha, okay.
